item.description: Pittsburgh benched the four-time MVP ahead of Friday's visit from Denver.

item.title: The ‘French Milei’? Presidential candidate David Lisnard aims to reshape France’s right wing
item.description: Having secured reelection victory Wednesday as leader of France's mayors, Cannes Mayor David Lisnard turns once more to build on his recent bid for the Élysée. As his Nouvelle Énergie movement gains momentum, questions swirl over whether his campaign will reshape the French political landscape, or if his party will ultimately cosy up to the far right ahead of France’s 2027 race to the polls.

item.title: Stocks mixed as Wall Street erases sharp decline: Nvidia down 6%
item.description: The seesaw trading came amid a tumultuous stretch on Wall Street.

item.title: Federal officials say 'zero' airborne lead detected after Iowa munitions blast
item.description: The Army detonated several tons of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Iowa.

item.title: Group of Senate Democrats push to add freshman to leadership
item.description: Several Democratic senators have been signaling this move, saying the party needs to acknowledge the diverse class of incoming freshman that catapulted the party to victory in November.

item.title: Turkey's deadly factory blast: 'Investing in safety costs more than letting people die'
item.description: An explosion at a steel factory on November 9 in Turkey's Aliaga, near Izmir, killed 19 people. This tragedy follows several others and highlights the issues surrounding workers’ safety in Turkey, our Observers say. They also condemn the repressive responses from the government and the company.

item.title: WATCH: DoorDash aims to deliver 2M meals to food banks for free
item.description: Daniel Riff, head of global food access programs for DoorDash, discusses the company's initiative.

item.title: Paris takes on masculinist movements
item.description: As masculinist movements face their first major trial in Paris, the city has announced several initiatives to combat this ideology. The campaign aims to call attention to the real-world danger posed by misogynist groups online. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler takes a closer look.

item.title: WATCH: 'Dancing with the Stars' superfan gets special surprise
item.description: A lucky superfan receives two tickets to the "Dancing with the Stars" live show on Feb. 16, including a behind-the-scenes tour, a meet-and-greet and exclusive merchandise.

item.title: WATCH: Best and worst times to drive
item.description: ABC News' Rhiannon Ally provides the latest updates on the road as gas prices drop, offering some relief for drivers this Thanksgiving.

item.title: 'Free' land and thriving businesses: French village defies rural decline
item.description: As France's mayors gather in Paris for their annual convention, the decline in living standards and public services in both urban and rural areas is high on the agenda. Rural mayors, in particular, are concerned about the shrinking populations of their communities. But one small French town bucking the trend is Parlan, in the Cantal region, where the population has doubled and local services have flourished thanks to an offer of virtually free plots of land.

item.title: Moldova launches national preparedness campaign after drone incursions
item.description: Moldova is urging its citizens to prepare for emergencies as the war in neighbouring Ukraine brings new risks across its border. The “Moldova Ready” campaign, launched in Chisinau, includes a display of the remains of a drone carrying 52kg of explosives after it crashed in the country last month. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

item.title: Top Spanish court closes case against Catalan separatist leader
item.description: Spain's Supreme Court has applied a controversial amnesty law to former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, closing criminal proceedings against him over his role in the region's failed 2017 independence bid. The ruling, which comes ahead of a snap general election on Sunday, marks the final step in the implementation of the amnesty law, passed by parliament in 2024.

item.title: Huang's return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
item.description: A rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive faded on Tuesday, with the company's shares falling as doubts persisted over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom. After vaulting more than 30 percent on Monday following Huang's shock comeback, Nvidia fell almost six percent Tuesday. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

item.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
item.description: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production – the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The new tariffs will need to undergo a period of public comment before taking effect. The new levies target some of the United States' largest trading partners. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Iranian family seeks release of twin sisters facing death penalty and 25 years in prison
item.description: Twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi are awaiting their sentences in Iran. They were arrested in January 2026, at the age of just 19, for taking part in protests against the Iranian regime. Taraneh is facing the death penalty, while Romina has been sentenced to 25 years in prison. Their family has been campaigning for their release.

item.title: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000
item.description: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests some 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency.

item.title: Iowa: Toxic dust fears as US Army blows up 10,000 pounds of explosives
item.description: An enormous explosion rang out across rural Iowa Tuesday as the US military carried out the controlled detonation of some 10,000 pounds of lead azide. US officials say the material, which was once used as a detonator in munitions, had become unstable and was at risk at risk of spontaneous explosion. But the risk of a toxic cloud of lead dust spreading out from the blast zone has caused public safety fears among locals.

item.title: Colombia: Security forces rescue hostages in supermarket siege
item.description: Some 25 people being held hostage by gunmen in a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, were freed Tuesday after security forces stormed the building. One assailant was killed during the operation but no hostages were injured.

item.title: US Army detonates lead explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
item.description: The US Army on Wednesday blew up 5 tons of lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in Iowa despite community backlash over fears of environmental contamination. The detonation was postponed three times, but got the green light after a federal appeals court this week found the US Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards to minimise the dispersal of lead dust.

item.title: WATCH: Thanksgiving travel rush underway
item.description: Major airlines already offering travel waivers in the wake of the Thanksgiving travel rush as a collision between a plane and catering truck at JFK airport creates delays.

item.title: 'We need to stop the war in Iran': US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Democratic Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal laid out her priorities for the new Congress: ending the war in Iran, tackling the cost-of-living crisis, curbing political corruption and holding the Trump administration accountable for its immigration crackdown. She also called for the "complete" dismantling of the US federal immigration agency ICE and backed an end to US military funding for Israel.

item.title: 'The threat is finally real': Judge rips White House 'weaponization'
item.description: A D.C. magistrate judge has issued a scathing written order ripping the Trump administration for what he described as the blatant "weaponization" of law enforcement.

item.title: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
item.description: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: French Mayors Conference: 2027 Elysée hopeful Lisnard reelected association president
item.description: The Mayor of Cannes, David Lisnard, has been re-elected president of the Association of Mayors of France, securing a comfortable victory in a vote announced on Wednesday. Lisnard is also a candidate in next year's French presidential election. For more on what his re-election could mean, FRANCE 24's James André reports from the Association of Mayors' convention in Paris.

item.title: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday. The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.

item.title: Moldova issues emergency kit guide, prepares citizens for possible expansion of Ukraine war
item.description: As the war in Ukraine has highlighted the importance of civilian preparedness, Moldova has launched its own emergency readiness programme. Medicine, batteries and three days' worth of food are among the essentials citizens are encouraged to keep at hand, in case they need to leave at a moment's notice.

item.title: Exiled Catalan separatist Puigdemont to return to Spain after election
item.description: Catalan separatist ​and former regional leader Carles Puigdemont said on Wednesday he would end nearly a decade of self-imposed exile in Belgium and return to Spain on December 12, ​after ‌this weekend's national election. Puigdemont, whose legal troubles in ⁠Spain are over after the Supreme Court earlier this week applied an amnesty law to shelve the ‌criminal case against him, said at a televised news conference from ⁠Brussels that he would unveil his proposal for a renewed Catalan independence push on December 17. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

item.title: 'Paper Tiger': Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver shine in Russian mob thriller
item.description: This week on arts24, Emma Jones and Dheepthika Laurent discuss the latest film releases. We start with "Paper Tiger", a Russian mob thriller starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller. It is a return to familiar crime thriller territory for James Gray, the director behind "Little Odessa" and "The Yards".

item.title: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Wednesday reignited global trade tensions by proposing new tariffs on some of the largest US trading partners, including the EU, Japan and Taiwan. China could be slapped with a 20 percent tariff, a senior official said. The announcement came weeks after a cost-of-living crisis landed the Republicans a sweeping defeat in the US midterms.

item.title: Melania Trump reunites seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children with families
item.description: The White House says Melania Trump has helped return a seventh group of Ukrainian and Russian children to their families

item.title: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia
item.description: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

item.title: California braces for flooding threat from huge tides, El Nino
item.description: Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fueled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding during the busiest US travel week of the year. The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, which forecasters warned could push seawater into low-lying areas on Wednesday and Thursday.

item.title: 'Historic' space mission: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying Pakistani astronaut
item.description: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit. The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s crewed space program.

item.title: 'Utterly broken' mother pays tribute to son found fatally injured in hospital car park
item.description: An "utterly broken" mother has paid tribute to her son, who died after being found seriously injured in a hospital car park in a suspected murder.

item.title: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
item.description: Security forces rescued all the hostages held for nearly a day at a supermarket in the northern Colombian tourist city of Cartagena, President Abelardo de la Espriella said early Wednesday. The president said that the men were “common criminals” who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck. The hostage situation broke out as Colombia is experiencing a wave of attacks by rebel groups on government targets.
